newsitem.title: USA: Mobil has raised production rise targets.
newsitem.headline: Mobil has raised production rise targets.

text.p: Mobil Corp said Tuesday that company officials told investment analysts in New York last week that it has increased its production growth targets.

It said the analysts were told Mobil expects to grow oil and natural gas production by an average of 3.5 percent per year through the early years of the next century, while replacing its reserve base by more than 100 percent annually.

Paul J. Hoenmans, Executive Vice President and a member of Mobil's board, told the analysts these projections are above Mobil's earlier annual growth targets of at least two percent for production and 100 percent for reserves, it said.

"Mobil has a strong upstream track record," said Hoenmans. "Over the past five years, we have been the industry leader in return on capital employed and a top performer in production growth, reserve replacement and the cost of finding and development.

"At the same time, we have been addressing some areas of concern which were identified previously. These include the need to add significant new production and earnings sources to our base business and to restructure our North American operations."

New production in the future is expected to come primarily from seven sources being actively progressed now, Mobil said. These include Tengiz in Kazakstan, Australia's Ampolex, South America, liquefied natural gas, West Africa, Eastern Canada and Norway.
To reach its upstream growth goals, Mobil said, the company estimates it will invest an average of about $3.5 billion per year of capital between 1997 and 2000.
This compares to about $3 billion per year in 1995 and 1996, excluding the almost $2 billion spent for its share of the Tengiz oil field and the acquisition of Ampolex in 1996.

Plans call for exploration expense to continue to be budgeted at $400 to $500 million per year, but actual spending could vary depending on the economics of exploration versus acquisition opportunities.
"Our upstream operations have a strong, profitable base which we will continue to improve and high-grade," Hoenmans concluded.

"Our seven growth sources will add 6.8 billion barrels oil equivalent to Mobil's resource base this year and over 800 (barrels per day) oil equivalent of new production over the next ten years. Our focus is to achieve the projected growth from these sources, while continuing to pursue attractive opportunities which become available to us."
